blocks.body: How do we know the height of Mount Everest without climbing it? How do surveyors measure the width of a river without crossing it? The answer is **Similar Triangles**! When two triangles have the same shape but different sizes, they are called similar. This powerful idea of similarity lets us solve real-world measurement problems using just geometry.
blocks.body_hi: हम माउंट एवरेस्ट की ऊँचाई बिना चढ़े कैसे जानते हैं? सर्वेक्षक नदी को पार किए बिना उसकी चौड़ाई कैसे मापते हैं? उत्तर है **समरूप त्रिभुज**! जब दो त्रिभुजों का आकार समान हो लेकिन आकार भिन्न हो, तो उन्हें समरूप कहते हैं।
blocks.body_gu: માઉન્ટ એવરેસ્ટની ઊંચાઈ ચઢ્યા વિના કેવી રીતે જાણીએ? સર્વેક્ષક નદી ઓળ્યા વિના તેની પહોળાઈ કેવી રીતે માપે? જવાબ છે **સમરૂપ ત્રિકોણ**! બે ત્રિકોણ સમાન આકારના હોય પણ અલગ કદ — તેમને સમ-રૂપ (Similar) કહે.

blocks.body:
**Key Concepts in This Chapter:**

1. **Similar Figures:** Same shape, not necessarily same size.
2. **Basic Proportionality Theorem (BPT / Thales Theorem):** If a line is drawn parallel to one side of a triangle, it divides the other two sides in the same ratio: AD/DB = AE/EC.
3. **Converse of BPT:** If a line divides two sides in the same ratio, it is parallel to the third side.
4. **AA Similarity:** If two angles of one triangle = two angles of another → triangles are similar.
5. **SSS Similarity:** If all three sides are in the same ratio → similar.
6. **SAS Similarity:** One angle equal + sides including it in same ratio → similar.
7. **Areas of Similar Triangles:** Ratio of areas = Square of ratio of corresponding sides.
8. **Pythagoras Theorem:** In a right triangle, hypotenuse² = base² + height².
blocks.body_hi:
**मुख्य अवधारणाएँ:**
1. समरूप आकृतियाँ: समान आकार, आवश्यक नहीं समान आकार।
2. BPT: DE||BC तो AD/DB = AE/EC।
3. AA, SSS, SAS समरूपता मापदंड।
4. समरूप त्रिभुजों के क्षेत्रफलों का अनुपात = संगत भुजाओं के अनुपात का वर्ग।
5. पाइथागोरस: कर्ण² = आधार² + ऊँचाई²।
blocks.body_gu:
**મૂળ ખ્યાલો:**
1. સમ-રૂપ આકૃતિ: સમ આકાર, ન borne 1 same size.
2. BPT: DE||BC → AD/DB = AE/EC.
3. AA, SSS, SAS સદ-rl.
4. AreaRatio = SideRatio².
5. Pythagoras: hyp² = base² + height².

blocks.body:
**EXERCISE 6.1 — Similar Figures (Basic Concepts)**

This exercise tests whether you understand the basic definition of similarity:
- Two figures are similar if they have the same shape (corresponding angles equal AND corresponding sides in proportion).
- All circles are similar. All squares are similar. All equilateral triangles are similar.
- But: Congruent figures are always similar. Similar figures need NOT be congruent.
blocks.body_hi:
**अभ्यास 6.1 — समरूप आकृतियाँ**

समरूपता की मूल परिभाषा: सभी वृत्त समरूप हैं। सभी वर्ग समरूप हैं। सभी समबाहु त्रिभुज समरूप हैं।
blocks.body_gu:
**ক. 6.1 — সমরূপ আকৃতি**

বधী वर्तुळ सभरूप. বধী ছোল. সব સमবাহু. সমরূপতা ≠ সর্বাঙ্গসমতা.

blocks.question: Ex 6.1 Q1(i): All circles are _____. (congruent / similar)
blocks.question_hi: अभ्यास 6.1 प्र1(i): सभी वृत्त _____ हैं। (सर्वांगसम / समरूप)
blocks.question_gu: ক. 6.1 Q1(i): બધા ও _____ ছে. (সর্বাঙ্গ / সমরূপ)
blocks.explanation: All circles have the same shape (round) but different sizes. So they are SIMILAR. They are NOT congruent because they have different radii.
blocks.explanation_hi: सभी वृत्त एक ही आकार के होते हैं लेकिन अलग-अलग आकार के। इसलिए वे समरूप हैं।
blocks.explanation_gu: বধী वर्तुळ সম-shape পण अलग size. তেथী Similar.

blocks.question: Ex 6.1 Q1(ii): All squares are _____. (similar / congruent)
blocks.explanation: All squares have the same shape (all angles 90°, all sides equal ratio) but different sizes. So all squares are SIMILAR. They are congruent only if they have the same side length.
blocks.explanation_hi: सभी वर्ग समान आकार के हैं, इसलिए समरूप हैं।

blocks.question: Ex 6.1 Q1(iii): All _____ triangles are similar. (isosceles / equilateral)
blocks.question_hi: अभ्यास 6.1 प्र1(iii): सभी _____ त्रिभुज समरूप हैं।
blocks.explanation: All equilateral triangles have all angles = 60°. So corresponding angles are always equal → all equilateral triangles are similar. Isosceles triangles can have different base angles, so not all are similar.
blocks.explanation_hi: सभी समबाहु त्रिभुजों के सभी कोण 60° होते हैं → सभी समरूप हैं।

blocks.question: Ex 6.1 Q1(iv): Two polygons with same number of sides are similar if corresponding angles are _____ and corresponding sides are _____.
blocks.question_hi: अभ्यास 6.1 प्र1(iv): समान भुजाओं वाले दो बहुभुज समरूप हैं यदि संगत कोण _____ हों और संगत भुजाएँ _____ हों।
blocks.question_gu: ক. 6.1 Q1(iv): সम भुजा बहुभुज → कोण _____ আne भुजा _____.
blocks.explanation: For two polygons to be similar: (a) corresponding angles must be EQUAL and (b) corresponding sides must be PROPORTIONAL (in the same ratio).
blocks.explanation_hi: समरूपता के लिए: (a) संगत कोण समान हों और (b) संगत भुजाएँ आनुपातिक हों।

blocks.body:
**EXERCISE 6.2 — Basic Proportionality Theorem (Thales Theorem)**

**Theorem 6.1 (BPT):** If a line DE is drawn parallel to BC in triangle ABC, intersecting AB at D and AC at E, then:
**AD/DB = AE/EC**

**Converse (Theorem 6.2):** If a line divides two sides of a triangle in the same ratio, it is parallel to the third side.

**Remember:** BPT gives proportional division, NOT equal division. D divides AB, E divides AC in the same ratio.
blocks.body_hi:
**अभ्यास 6.2 — आधारभूत आनुपातिकता प्रमेय**

यदि DE || BC तो AD/DB = AE/EC

उलटा: यदि AD/DB = AE/EC तो DE || BC
blocks.body_gu:
**ক. 6.2 — BPT**

DE || BC → AD/DB = AE/EC
उलटु: AD/DB = AE/EC → DE || BC

blocks.question: Ex 6.2 Q1(i): In triangle ABC, DE || BC. If AD=1.5 cm, DB=3 cm, AE=1 cm, find EC.
blocks.question_hi: अभ्यास 6.2 प्र1(i): ΔABC में DE || BC। AD=1.5 cm, DB=3 cm, AE=1 cm। EC ज्ञात करें।
blocks.explanation: By BPT: AD/DB = AE/EC → 1.5/3 = 1/EC → EC = 1 × 3/1.5 = 2 cm.

blocks.question: Ex 6.2 Q1(ii): In triangle ABC, DE || BC. If DB=7.2 cm, AE=1.8 cm, EC=5.4 cm, find AD.
blocks.question_hi: अभ्यास 6.2 प्र1(ii): ΔABC में DE || BC। DB=7.2 cm, AE=1.8 cm, EC=5.4 cm। AD ज्ञात करें।

blocks.question: Ex 6.2 Q2(i): PE=3.9, EQ=3, PF=3.6, FR=2.4. Is EF || QR?
options: No, EF is not parallel to QR
blocks.explanation: For EF || QR, we need PE/EQ = PF/FR. PE/EQ = 3.9/3 = 1.3 and PF/FR = 3.6/2.4 = 1.5. Since 1.3 ≠ 1.5, EF is NOT parallel to QR.
blocks.explanation_hi: PE/EQ = 1.3 और PF/FR = 1.5। 1.3 ≠ 1.5, इसलिए EF || QR नहीं।

blocks.question: Ex 6.2 Q2(ii): PE=4, QE=4.5, PF=8, RF=9. Is EF || QR?
blocks.question_hi: अभ्यास 6.2 प्र2(ii): PE=4, QE=4.5, PF=8, RF=9। क्या EF || QR?
blocks.explanation: PE/QE = 4/4.5 = 8/9. PF/RF = 8/9. Since PE/QE = PF/RF, by converse of BPT, EF || QR.
blocks.explanation_hi: PE/QE = 4/4.5 = PF/RF = 8/9। अनुपात समान → EF || QR।

blocks.question: Ex 6.2 Q2(iii): PQ=1.28, PR=2.56, PE=0.18, PF=0.36. Is EF || QR?
blocks.explanation: PE/PQ = 0.18/1.28 = 9/64. PF/PR = 0.36/2.56 = 9/64. Since PE/PQ = PF/PR = 9/64, by converse BPT, EF || QR.

blocks.question: Ex 6.2 Q9: ABCD is a trapezium with AB || DC. Diagonals intersect at O. Show AO/BO = CO/DO. Which theorem is used?
blocks.question_hi: अभ्यास 6.2 प्र9: ABCD समलंब है, AB || DC। विकर्ण O पर मिलते हैं। AO/BO = CO/DO सिद्ध करें।
blocks.question_gu: ক. 6.2 Q9: ABCD trapezium, AB||DC. Diagonals O. AO/BO = CO/DO. কোনো प्रমेय?
options: BPT applied in triangles AOB and COD
options_hi: BPT त्रिभुज AOB और COD पर
blocks.explanation: In ΔAOB and ΔCOD, since AB||DC, alternate angles are equal: ∠OAB=∠OCD and ∠OBA=∠ODC. So ΔAOB~ΔCOD (AA). Therefore AO/CO = BO/DO, i.e., AO/BO = CO/DO.

blocks.body:
**EXERCISE 6.3 — Similarity Criteria (AA, SSS, SAS)**

**AA Criterion:** If two angles of one triangle equal two angles of another → similar.
**SSS Criterion:** If sides of two triangles are in the same ratio → similar.
**SAS Criterion:** One angle equal + including sides proportional → similar.

**Important properties of similar triangles:**
- Corresponding sides are in the same ratio (scale factor)
- All corresponding angles are equal
- Ratio of areas = (ratio of sides)²
- Ratio of medians = ratio of sides
blocks.body_hi:
**अभ्यास 6.3 — समरूपता मापदंड**

AA: दो कोण समान → समरूप
SSS: तीनों भुजाएँ समानुपाती → समरूप
SAS: एक कोण + आसन्न भुजाएँ समानुपाती → समरूप
blocks.body_gu:
**ক. 6.3 — Similarity criteria**

AA: 2 angles equal → similar
SSS: सब sides ratio same → similar
SAS: 1 angle + sides proportional → similar

blocks.question: Ex 6.3 Q2: In ΔODC ~ ΔOBA, ∠BOC=125° and ∠CDO=70°. Find ∠DOC, ∠DCO and ∠OAB.
blocks.question_hi: अभ्यास 6.3 प्र2: ΔODC ~ ΔOBA, ∠BOC=125°, ∠CDO=70°। ∠DOC, ∠DCO और ∠OAB ज्ञात करें।
blocks.explanation: ∠DOC = 180° – ∠BOC = 180° – 125° = 55° (linear pair). In ΔODC: ∠DCO = 180° – 55° – 70° = 55°. Since ΔODC ~ ΔOBA, ∠OAB = ∠ODC = 70°.

blocks.question: Ex 6.3 Q15: A pole of 6m casts a 4m shadow. At same time, a tower casts a 28m shadow. Find height of tower.
blocks.question_hi: अभ्यास 6.3 प्र15: 6 मीटर का खंभा 4 मीटर की छाया डालता है। उसी समय एक टॉवर 28 मीटर की छाया डालता है। टॉवर की ऊँचाई?
blocks.question_gu: ক. 6.3 Q15: 6m ডাँड→4m shadow. Tower→28m shadow. Tower height?
blocks.explanation: The pole and its shadow form a right triangle. The tower and its shadow form a similar triangle (same sun angle). By AA: 6/4 = height/28 → height = 6×28/4 = 42 m.

blocks.question: Ex 6.3 Q1: Two triangles have angles 80°,60°,40° and 80°,60°,40°. What similarity criterion applies?
blocks.question_gu: ক. 6.3 Q1: Two triangles → 80°,60°,40° each. Criterion?
blocks.explanation: All three corresponding angles are equal. By AA (two angles equal is sufficient → third automatically equal by angle sum property), the triangles are similar.
blocks.explanation_hi: तीनों संगत कोण समान → AA समरूपता।

blocks.question: Ex 6.3 Q7: Altitudes AD and CE of ΔABC intersect at P. Show that ΔAEP ~ ΔCDP. Which criterion?
blocks.question_hi: अभ्यास 6.3 प्र7: ΔABC की ऊँचाइयाँ AD और CE, P पर मिलती हैं। ΔAEP ~ ΔCDP। कौन-सा मापदंड?
blocks.question_gu: ক. 6.3 Q7: Altitudes AD, CE, P par milta. ΔAEP ~ ΔCDP. Criterion?
blocks.explanation: ∠AEP = 90° (CE is altitude) and ∠CDP = 90° (AD is altitude). Also ∠APE = ∠CPD (vertically opposite angles). So ΔAEP ~ ΔCDP by AA.

blocks.question: Ex 6.3 Q13: D is on BC of ΔABC, and ∠ADC = ∠BAC. Show that CA² = CB.CD. Which similarity is used?
blocks.question_hi: अभ्यास 6.3 प्र13: D, ΔABC के BC पर है, ∠ADC = ∠BAC। CA² = CB.CD सिद्ध करें।
options: AA: ΔABC ~ ΔDAC → CA/CD = CB/CA → CA² = CB·CD
blocks.explanation: In ΔABC and ΔDAC: ∠BAC=∠ADC (given) and ∠C=∠C (common). So ΔABC~ΔDAC (AA). Therefore CA/CD = CB/CA → CA² = CB·CD.

blocks.body:
💡 **Important Theorem: Areas of Similar Triangles**

If two triangles are similar with a scale factor of k (ratio of sides), then:
**Ratio of their Areas = k²** (square of scale factor)

Example: If ΔABC ~ ΔDEF with AB/DE = 3/2, then:
Area(ΔABC)/Area(ΔDEF) = (3/2)² = 9/4

This theorem is called the 'Areas of Similar Triangles Theorem' and it states:
**ar(ABC)/ar(DEF) = (AB/DE)² = (BC/EF)² = (AC/DF)²**
blocks.body_hi:
💡 **क्षेत्रफलों का अनुपात = भुजाओं के अनुपात का वर्ग**

यदि ΔABC ~ ΔDEF तो:
ar(ABC)/ar(DEF) = (AB/DE)² = (BC/EF)² = (CA/FD)²
blocks.body_gu:
💡 **Area ratio = Side ratio squared**

ΔABC ~ ΔDEF → ar(ABC)/ar(DEF) = (AB/DE)²

blocks.body:
💡 **Pythagoras Theorem:**
In a right triangle with hypotenuse c and legs a, b:
**c² = a² + b²**

**Converse:** If c² = a² + b² then the angle opposite to c is 90°.

Common Pythagorean triplets: (3,4,5), (5,12,13), (8,15,17), (7,24,25)

**Proof uses similar triangles:** When the altitude from the right angle is drawn to the hypotenuse, three similar triangles are formed.
blocks.body_hi:
💡 **पाइथागोरस प्रमेय:**
समकोण त्रिभुज में: c² = a² + b²
उलटा: c² = a² + b² → कोण C = 90°
सामान्य: (3,4,5), (5,12,13), (8,15,17)
blocks.body_gu:
💡 **Pythagoras:**
Right triangle: c² = a² + b²
Converse: c² = a² + b² → ∠C = 90°
Common triplets: (3,4,5), (5,12,13)

blocks.question: Theorem: If ΔABC ~ ΔDEF with AB/DE = 3/5, what is the ratio of their areas?
blocks.question_hi: प्रमेय: यदि ΔABC ~ ΔDEF और AB/DE = 3/5, तो उनके क्षेत्रफलों का अनुपात?
blocks.explanation: Ratio of areas = (ratio of corresponding sides)² = (3/5)² = 9/25. So ar(ABC):ar(DEF) = 9:25.

blocks.question: Pythagoras Theorem: In right-angled ΔABC (right angle at B), AB=3, BC=4, AC=?
blocks.question_hi: पाइथागोरस: ΔABC में ∠B=90°, AB=3, BC=4, AC=?
blocks.explanation: By Pythagoras: AC² = AB² + BC² = 9 + 16 = 25. AC = 5. This is the famous 3-4-5 right triangle.

blocks.question: Converse of Pythagoras: A triangle has sides 5, 12, 13. Is it right-angled?
blocks.question_hi: पाइथागोरस का उलटा: एक त्रिभुज की भुजाएँ 5, 12, 13 हैं। क्या यह समकोण त्रिभुज है?
options: Yes, right angle at side opposite to 13
blocks.explanation: Check: 13² = 5² + 12²? → 169 = 25 + 144 = 169. YES! By converse of Pythagoras, the angle opposite to the longest side (13) is 90°.

blocks.question: Ex 6.3 Q (similar to Example 7): A girl 90 cm tall walks at 1.2 m/s from a 3.6 m lamp. After 4 sec, shadow length?
blocks.question_hi: Ex 6.3 उदाहरण: 90 cm लड़की 1.2 m/s से 3.6 m के दीपक से दूर जाती है। 4 सेकंड बाद छाया की लंबाई?
blocks.explanation: Distance walked = 1.2×4 = 4.8 m. Let shadow = x. By AA similarity of the two triangles formed: (4.8+x)/x = 3.6/0.9 = 4. So 4.8+x = 4x → 3x=4.8 → x=1.6 m.

blocks.body:
📋 **Chapter 6 Summary:**

1. Similar figures: Same shape, possibly different size.
2. **BPT:** DE||BC in ΔABC → AD/DB = AE/EC.
3. **Converse BPT:** AD/DB = AE/EC → DE||BC.
4. **Similarity Criteria:** AA / SSS / SAS.
5. **Area Theorem:** ar(similar Δ)/ar(similar Δ) = (side ratio)².
6. **Pythagoras:** hyp² = base² + height² in right Δ.
7. **Converse Pythagoras:** c²=a²+b² → right angle at C.
blocks.body_hi:
📋 **अध्याय 6 सारांश:**
1. BPT: DE||BC → AD/DB = AE/EC
2. AA/SSS/SAS → समरूपता
3. क्षेत्रफल अनुपात = (भुजा अनुपात)²
4. पाइथागोरस: कर्ण² = आधार² + ऊँचाई²
blocks.body_gu:
📋 **ক. 6 Summary:**
1. BPT: DE||BC → AD/DB=AE/EC
2. AA/SSS/SAS → similar
3. Area ratio = (side ratio)²
4. Pythagoras: hyp² = base² + height²
